title: pollen
subtitle: 𓇢𓆸 the world's radio, carried on the wind, scattered as grains · for monome norns
about: A live granular instrument for the world's radio. pollen tunes into a station somewhere on Earth, catches it on a reel (a loop of the last few seconds, drawn as tape) and scatters it as grains: you choose how far back they reach, how many, how long, how high, and how they're colored. The wind carries you to the next station, near or far, when you drift (K3 on the wind part), or on its own if you give it a pace. Press Start sound and listen.
more: pollen is a script for monome norns, a small computer for making sound. What plays here is the real script, running in your browser: the stations are live, from radio-browser.info (here, only the ones whose servers allow a web page to play them), and the engine is rebuilt in Web Audio with the reverb on the same Mutable Instruments code a norns plays. The screen shows pictures, not numbers.

controls.does: pick a part: wind, catch, scatter, tint, tone or air
shape that part; the two knobs show their names while you turn them
a gesture: drift, press the reel, a burst of grains, play them backwards, a fade, hold the haze
choose a variety: the wind, the reel's length, the grains' shape, the scale, the media
the heads: how many read the reel (catch), how far apart they play in the scale (tint)
peek at every part, where its knobs are, and the station

actions.label: Drift
actions.title: The wind carries you to another station

gallery_intro: Six parts, each a knob pair, a gesture and a variety. Turn E1 to pick the part, E2 and E3 to shape it, K3 for its gesture, and hold K2 while turning E2 for its variety. Hold K1 to see every part's knobs at once.

gallery.title: wind
gallery.alt: The wind part: pace and reach, the globe on the left
gallery.text: When and where the radio moves on. Pace: how often (still, or every 10 minutes to every 30 seconds). Reach: how far, from the next town to across an ocean. K3 drifts now. The variety is the wind: breeze, trade wind, eddy, gust or far side.

gallery.title: catch
gallery.alt: The catch part: three heads, a bracket for each under the tape
gallery.text: The reel the radio is caught on. Position: how far back the grains read, from almost live to seconds ago. Feedback: grains recorded back onto the reel, into smears and drones. K3 presses the reel (it holds what it has). The variety is its length, 4 to 60 s; hold K2 and turn E3 for up to four heads.

gallery.title: scatter
gallery.alt: The scatter part: density and size
gallery.text: The grains. Density: from one every two seconds to 40 a second. Size: from a 20 ms click to a 2 s wash. K3 is a burst. The variety is the grain's shape: bell, pluck or block.

gallery.title: tint
gallery.alt: The tint part: pitch and spread
gallery.text: The grains' pitch, snapped to a scale. Pitch: two octaves down to two up. Spread: how far each grain wanders, and past the middle some play backwards. K3 flips them all. The variety is the scale; hold K2 and turn E3 to spread the heads into a chord.

gallery.title: tone
gallery.alt: The tone part: color and drive
gallery.text: The color. Color: one filter knob, a low-pass to the left, a high-pass to the right, open in the middle. Drive: clean to crunchy. K3 is a shortwave fade. The variety is the media, after Beads: digital, vintage, clean tape or dirty tape.

gallery.title: air
gallery.alt: The air part: space and mix
gallery.text: The space and the mix. Space: how much goes to the reverb, and how big it is. Mix: the station alone, the grains alone, or both. K3 holds the reverb's haze.
